 Irish Take Down Auburn Tigers In 78 73 Victory 
 Jeffrey Myers Featured in this article Brady Koehler Logan Imes Braeden Shrewsberry Jonathan Sanderson Logan Duncomb Braeden Smith Irish Take Down Auburn Tigers In 78-73 Victory
 ND finishes with 2-1 record at Players Era 8, improving to 6-1 on the season November 19, 2026 Twitter Facebook Email Featured in this article Brady Koehler Logan Imes Braeden Shrewsberry Jonathan Sanderson Logan Duncomb Braeden Smith Box Score 
 PDF Box 
 LAS VEGAS - The (RV) Notre Dame men's basketball team (6-1) took down the Auburn Tigers (3-3) in a 78-73 victory as the Irish completed a 2-1 week at the Players Era 8 and continue to be big early season movers in KenPom. 
 The Irish were led yet again by veteran point guard, Braeden Smith , who finished the night with 23 points and now 53 points on the week in Vegas. He finished the night 7-11 from the floor and 8-9 from the free throw line, while grabbing 8 rebounds and dishing out 4 assists. Smith shot 17-for-22 over the last two games. He dished out 15 assists over the last three. 
 Senior Braeden Shrewsberry also poured in 18 points on a 7-14 shooting night as he finished the week with 51 points at the Players Era 8. 
 They were followed by sophomore Brady Koehler with 15 points and 8 boards, shooting 4-10 from floor and 3-5 from behind the arc. Koehler had himself a trip out west as he led all Irish players with 59 points on the week in Vegas. He averaged 7.0 rebounds per game over the three games and was 10-of-16 from three-point range. 
 The Irish had three different players drop 15+ PTS in the win over Auburn ☘️ This is their fourth game this season with three players each with 15+ PTS, the most in D-I 🔥 https://t.co/hXxS7VHUy4
— ESPN Insights (@ESPNInsights) November 20, 2026 Fifth-year Logan Duncomb also finished the night in double-digits as he finished with 10 points in the win, shooting 4-5 from the floor, while also contributing a pair of rebounds and three assists.
 The Irish finished the night shooting 25-51 at a clip of 49.0 percent, while going 8-31 (38.1 percent) from behind the arc. Auburn finished with a 22-54 shooting performance (40.7 percent) from the floor and finished shooting 31.0 percent on 9-29 shooting from three. 
 It was a game of free throws, as the Irish and Tigers shot a combined 33 in the second half for a total of 55 on the night. The Irish finished the night 20-27 from the line and Tigers were there with them, going 20-28 from the charity stripe.
 Thus, over the last three games, the Irish averaged 88.7 ppg on 54.8 percent shooting from the floor. They averaged 9.7 threes per game on a 41.4 percent clip from beyond the arc. 
 HOW IT HAPPENED  
 Notre Dame’s defense forced three turnovers in the opening minutes while four of the five starters contributed buckets, claiming a 14-8 lead The Irish had started 6-for-10 from the field, led by seven points from Braeden Smith . 
 Auburn countered with a 9-0 scoring run spanning 2:12, capturing their first lead of the game, up 17-14. 
 Next, Smith made it a 4-for-4 start from the field, while Shrewsberry connected on back-to-back buckets in the paint. At this point, the Irish were 9-of-18 from the floor, compared to the Tiger’s 8-for-18, and trailed 26-23.
 Out of the under-eight media timeout, Logan Imes drained a corner three, which was followed immediately by and-one from Logan Duncomb . This sequence ultimately spurred a 16-2 Irish scoring run in which they made five straight from the field. Meanwhile, Auburn went 1-of-9 from the field during said stretch.
 The Tigers garnered some momentum late with a quick 6-0 run to cut it to one possession but it was answered by a Shrewsberry triple. The senior guard then tacked on two free throws with nine seconds remaining, while Notre Dame’s defense earned a final stop, taking us to our halftime score of 42-36. 
 The Irish shot 50.0 percent from the floor on 13-26 shooting, while holding Auburn to 12-30 shooting at a 40.0 percent clip. The ND offense also took care of the ball, only coughing up two turnovers. Auburn notched a 6-1 offensive board advantage, in which they converted into nine second-chance points. 
 Shrewsberry led all players at halftime with 14 points on 5-9 shooting. He was followed by Smith with 13 points on a perfect 4-4 shooting performance, knocking down one triple and going 4-4 from the charity stripe. 
 At the under-16 media, it was 51-44 Notre Dame. The Irish had sunk four straight heading into the break, while the Tigers stayed close with a pair of triples. 
 Over the next four minutes, when Auburn cut it to one possession, Notre Dame answered with a score, getting contributions from both Shrewsberry and Imes. Yet, the Irish couldn’t muster any breathing room either, up just 55-52 with 11:39 remaining.
 Auburn tied the game with a corner three out of the break. Down on the other end, Jonathan Sanderson punched back with a triple. 
 It was back-and-forth scoring between the two squads as the Irish found answers from Koehler and Shrewsberry until it was tied up yet again at 65-all with 7:15 left. In fact, from 8:57 to the 3:57 media timeout, ND’s lead never exceeded three points, which also included four ties. Koehler scored seven points during this span. 
 Out of the timeout, the Irish sunk three free throws to extend their lead to five, but a finish at the rim from Auburn would make it a one-possession game yet again at 75-72 with 2:15 remaining.
 The Tigers went 2-8 from the charity stripe down the stretch, missing six consecutive free throws in the final four minutes of play. 
 With the Irish up 75-73 with 15 seconds left, Smith was relentless in his efforts against the Tigers as his tough, crafty finish at the rim extended the Irish lead to four. 
 BRAEDEN SMITH 🐶🐶🐶 #GoIrish☘️ https://t.co/7X7HpMPGGF
— Notre Dame Men's Basketball (@NDmbb) November 20, 2026 Notre Dame followed with a steal from Koehler on the Tigers’ inbounds pass with just under eight seconds remaining. Fouled on the steal, Koehler closed it out with one more free throw to secure the 78-73 win over Auburn. 
 UP NEXT 
 Plenty of opportunity awaits the Irish and it’ll all be at home. That’s right, Notre Dame will play nine straight inside Purcell Pavilion starting with Central Michigan on Tuesday, Nov. 24, at 8 p.m. ET.
